primary_claim: Supervised SAE-based steering methods (Supervised SAE-MELBO, SAE-Attribution) reliably reverse-engineer semantic backdoor triggers in toy Llama-3.1-8B backdoored models -- including succeeding in a blind auditing game -- but the same methods fail to recover interpretable triggers in more realistic settings (a synthetic-document-finetuned 'Banana' model and vanilla factual recall), suggesting trigger reconstruction is a promising but not yet practical alignment-auditing tool

effect.metric: backdoor action-rate on held-out triggered vs. benign prompts; interpretability of recovered SAE latents
effect.value: toy backdoors: 91-96% action-rate on 100 held-out triggered prompts vs. 0-1% on 100 held-out benign prompts, and Supervised SAE-MELBO/SAE-Attribution recovered interpretable trigger-related latents in all 3 toy models; both methods failed to find interpretable trigger latents in the realistic Banana and factual-recall settings

stated_future_work: try more simplistic token-level methods (e.g. which single input token most lowers loss on the backdoored action)
test other ways of interpreting steering vectors beyond SAE autointerp, e.g. max-activating data points, to remove dependence on SAEs
use internals-based targets such as the presence of a refusal direction or a coup probe
investigate how often a learned uninterpretable steering vector beats a manually chosen SAE latent combination in loss
give trigger reconstruction as a tool to an LLM conducting an automated alignment audit, and test it on real model quirks such as hiring bias
limitations_stated: toy backdoors use a fixed-string response, which may make finetuned mechanisms easier to reverse-engineer than real semantic backdoors
toy backdoor actions all relate to the trigger in some way, potentially making reconstruction easier
the 'realistic' Banana and factual-recall settings are still not fully adversarial/realistic
the Banana model was finetuned on all linear layers, potentially making the base Llama SAEs less applicable
supervised methods fail in realistic settings, finding steering vectors that induce the desired response but are not interpretable via SAE
quote: In toy settings, our best method reliably recovered the trigger. However, none of our methods succeeded in realistic scenarios. This suggests they are not yet viable for real-world auditing.
